title: GPU Programming & CUDA
tagline: Understand why GPUs are fast and write your own kernels: CUDA basics, memory, tiled matmul, Triton, and FlashAttention.
prereqs: Deep Learning (PyTorch and attention basics). C or C++ basics help. Needs an NVIDIA GPU or a free Colab GPU.

steps.title: CUDA clicks in 30 minutes
steps.why: Threads, blocks, and grids from a first principles view.

steps.title: Write your first CUDA kernel
steps.why: Launch a kernel and see the grid, block, and thread layout.

steps.title: GPU memory hierarchy
steps.why: Registers, shared memory, and global memory, and what each costs.

steps.title: Memory coalescing
steps.why: A small access-pattern change gives a large speedup.

steps.title: Tiled matrix multiplication
steps.why: Use shared memory to cut slow global reads.

steps.title: Profile CUDA kernels in PyTorch
steps.why: Find where time goes before you optimize.

steps.title: Custom PyTorch operators
steps.why: Hook your own CUDA or C++ code into PyTorch.

steps.title: Practitioner's guide to Triton
steps.why: Write fast kernels in Python-like code.

steps.title: A fast softmax kernel
steps.why: Fuse steps to avoid extra trips through memory.

steps.title: How FlashAttention works
steps.why: Tile attention so the big matrix never hits slow memory.

steps.title: FlashAttention from first principles in Triton
steps.why: Derive it and code the forward and backward pass.

projects: Write a vector add and a naive matmul in CUDA, then add tiling and chart the speedup.
Implement a fused softmax in Triton and benchmark it against PyTorch.
Profile one PyTorch model layer, find its bottleneck, and write up what you changed.
